title: Steel
objective: After this level you can explain how iron becomes steel and why steel changed building.
summary: Steel is iron with up to about 2 percent carbon; cast iron has more and is brittle. Bessemer's 1856 air blast burned out carbon, made steel cheap and changed building.

cards.headline: For most of history, steel was too costly to build with.
cards.body: Then, in 1856, Henry Bessemer patented a way to turn molten iron into steel in minutes, far more cheaply than before. Steel went from special to everyday. To see why that mattered so much, start with what separates steel from plain iron.

cards.headline: Steel is iron with a pinch of carbon
cards.body: Pure iron is soft. Add carbon and it gets much harder: steel is iron with up to about 2 percent carbon. Keep going, to 2 to 4 percent, and you get cast iron, which holds up fine when squeezed but is brittle and weak when pulled. Level 83's tension is cast iron's weak spot. Steel handles pulling well, which is why it goes inside reinforced concrete.

cards.headline: Bessemer's blast
cards.body: Bessemer blew air through molten iron fresh from the furnace. The oxygen burned out the extra carbon and other impurities, and those reactions gave off so much heat that the metal stayed molten with no added fuel. Steel in minutes, with the fire feeding itself. Cheap steel soon replaced iron in railroad rails and many other uses.

cards.fact: Steel is by far the most widely used material for building the world's infrastructure.
cards.context: Britannica says cheap Bessemer steel revolutionized building construction. Level 81's Home Insurance Building caught the moment: while it was going up, rolled-steel beams were substituted for some of its iron. Railways, frames and reinforced concrete all ride on the same pinch of carbon.

mascot.line: Look around: rails, beams, bars in the concrete. A little carbon went a very long way.

Cheap steel revolutionized building and rails

questions.prompt: What mainly separates steel from cast iron?

options.label: Steel is made from aluminum instead of iron
Steel contains more carbon than cast iron
Steel contains no carbon at all
options.rationale: That would be pure iron, which is soft.

options.label: Steel has less carbon: up to about 2 percent

questions.explanation: Steel is iron with up to about 2 percent carbon; cast iron has 2 to 4 percent.

questions.prompt: In the Bessemer process, why didn't the molten iron need extra fuel to stay hot?

options.label: It was heated by an electric current
options.rationale: The heat came from the reactions themselves.

options.label: Burning out the carbon released enough heat
The furnace walls stored heat from the day before
options.rationale: The blast's own reactions did it.

options.label: Cold air slowed the cooling down
options.rationale: The air fed reactions that released heat.

questions.explanation: Oxygen in the air blast burned out carbon and impurities, and the heat of those reactions kept the metal molten.

questions.prompt: Why did Bessemer's cheap steel matter for buildings like Level 81's Home Insurance Building?

options.label: It made a strong frame metal cheap enough to build with
It made brick walls thicker and stronger
It let buildings be made without any metal

questions.explanation: Cheap steel revolutionized building construction, and steel beams went into the Home Insurance Building's frame.
